# Working with real data

Up to here every sequence has been one you chose, and every file has been small
enough to read.

That changes now. This part introduces the libraries that working analysts
actually use, and the data arrives in the state data actually arrives in:
27,179 rows, twelve columns with unhelpful names, identifiers that are numbers
rather than gene names, and no instructions.

The skill this part teaches is not any one library. It's the habit of finding
out what's in a file before trusting anything you compute from it.
